content:
Apple is expected to hold an event next week on October 13 to unveil several new products. According to Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman, the product launch will take the form of "an event." Here's what he said.

Gurman pointed out that Apple will launch three new products at the October 13 event

It has been almost a month since last month's Apple event, which featured products such as the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo.

However, it appears the October event may be held as early as next Tuesday, October 13.

Gurman had previously reported that these three products would be released on October 13, but at the time he did not mention that a launch event would be held.

There has been much speculation about whether these new Home products warrant a dedicated launch event. John Gruber, for instance, believes the rumored HomePad will "absolutely not" be unveiled through a press release alone. He wrote: "If this product really launches, it has to be done with a keynote video paired with some kind of media event, and hands-on demo time."

And from Gurman's latest newsletter, he clearly agrees. The statement "Apple is planning to hold an event on Oct. 13" sounds pretty straightforward.

If the event does take place, invitations are expected to go out within the next day or two. Of course, unless incoming CEO John Ternus plans to completely overhaul the way products are launched, breaking with past precedent.

Do you think Apple's Home devices will be unveiled at an official October event, or will they only be announced via press release? Let us know in the comments.
